stories.summary: For many, Ratko Mladic represented the horrors of the Bosnian war. He was convicted of genocide for the Srebrenica massacre and other war crimes. On Thursday, he died in detention at The Hague.
stories.article_text_excerpt: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5JWvb Ratko Mladic, seen here in April 1993, was later found responsible for some of the most serious war crimes committed during the Bosnian war Image: Chris Helgren/REUTERS Advertisement More than 30 years after the end of the 1992-1995 war in Bosnia-Herzegovina, Srebrenica remains emblematic of its brutality. And no one is more closely linked to the genocide that took place in the small town in eastern Bosnia than Ratko Mladic , the former commander-in-chief of the Bosnian Serb army. Although the United Nations had declared Srebrenica a "safe area," Bosnian Serb forces attacked the town. Within just a few days in July 1995, they expelled women and children, then killed more than 8,300 unarmed Muslim boys and men in the nearby village of Potocari — on Mladic's direct orders, according to the verdict handed down by the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia (ICTY) in The Hague 22 years later. At the time, Srebrenica was the largest massacre in Europe since World War II . The ICTY classified it as genocide. stories.article_text_excerpt: One person died and around 15 people are missing or unaccounted for after a major flash flood at the Grand Canyon forced evacuations, swept large boulders into the Colorado River and knocked out the sole water pipeline that serves tourists and residents, the National Park Service said on Sunday.The body of a 46-year-old man was recovered late on Sunday evening near Crystal Rapids along the Colorado River, the park service said without providing additional details. Coroner’s officials were at the scene.Weekend flooding in Arizona’s Bright Angel Creek, which flows into the river, happened on Saturday afternoon.More than 60 people were evacuated from the depths of the canyon. The park service said it had yet to account for 15 people and asked anyone with details about hikers or campers in the canyon to get in touch.The Arizona Department of Public Safety was helping with additional evacuations on Sunday.Because the main water line was out of service, starting on Monday tourists won't be able to stay overnight at lodges and hotels within Grand Canyon National Park.
